item.title: Mia X Credits Birdman With Securing A “Big Bag” For Verzuz Appearance
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Mia X credited Birdman with making sure she was paid for Verzuz and described her decades-long friendship with Slim.
item.content:encoded:
Mia X credited Birdman with making sure she was properly paid for the Cash Money and No Limit Verzuz battle.

The No Limit veteran shared that account with WZAK’s Sam Sylk while discussing her longstanding ties to Cash Money.

She said she and Cash Money co-founder Slim have been close since 1993 and talk daily. She traced the idea of a feud between the labels largely to their fans.

“Slim is one of my best friends. I speak to him every single day since 1993. Baby made sure that the bag was big for me for Verzuz. We just really have an absolutely great relationship,” Mia X revealed.

Cash Money and No Limit faced off in a Verzuz battle in Las Vegas on October 25, 2025. Mia X represented No Limit during that performance.

Both labels grew out of New Orleans. Master P built No Limit while brothers Birdman and Slim established Cash Money.

Mia X became the first female rapper on No Limit. Her albums included Good Girl Gone Bad in 1995, Unlady Like in 1997 and Mama Drama in 1998. Her No Limit work also included appearances on Master P’s Ice Cream Man and Ghetto D.

Her connection with Master P began in 1994. She recalled working at a record store and performing in New Orleans when C-Murder saw her perform and recommended her to his brother. C-Murder was a regular customer at the store.

This summer, she also outlined plans to release music independently. In July, Mia X announced an album drawing on older unreleased songs and newer recordings.

The plans included collaborations with artists she had long admired and younger women rappers. She said she took charge of the project herself after continuing to write during her time away from the spotlight.

The two label families have since taken their catalogs on the road together with the “Cash Money & No Limit Tour.”

“I can tell you this. Mia X loves Cash Money from the bottom of my heart and the depths of my soul,” the rapper said.

The Cleveland stop is set for November 15 at Rocket Arena, with Mia X among the performers. She said she, Fiend and other acts open the show before the rest of the lineup performs.

Birdman, Master P, Juvenile, Mannie Fresh, B.G., Boosie and Silkk the Shocker are also on the Cleveland bill. The concert is set to begin at 7 p.m.

item.title: Eminem Publisher Demands $41 Million From Suno Over Alleged AI Copying
item.dc:creator: AllHipHop Staff
item.description: Eminem’s publishing dispute bring consent into focus and Elvis Presley representatives challenge synthetic performances.
item.content:encoded:
Eminem’s publisher sued AI music generator Suno in San Francisco federal court seeking approximately $41 million over allegations that the company used his songs without permission.

Eight Mile Style’s complaint puts some of Hip-Hop’s most recognizable compositions at the center of another fight over artificial intelligence. The publisher alleges Suno used copyrighted material to train its technology and enabled users to generate music and lyrics resembling Eminem’s work. Eminem himself is not a plaintiff.

The lawsuit arrived alongside a separate case from Elvis Presley’s rights owners that challenges both the alleged use of copyrighted songs and the reproduction of the singer’s voice. Both cases were brought in the Northern District of California. The accusations remain unproven.

Eight Mile Style controls rights to 269 Eminem compositions. Songs identified in reporting on the complaint include “Lose Yourself,” “Stan” and “The Real Slim Shady.”

The publisher seeks $150,000 for each composition, totaling $40.35 million, plus $672,000 over the alleged removal of copyright information. That brings the requested damages to approximately $41 million. The figure represents what the plaintiffs are pursuing rather than a court award.

The Presley case adds another question to the dispute: whether an AI platform can be held responsible for allowing users to reproduce an identifiable performer’s voice.

Elvis Presley Enterprises and affiliated rights holders allege Suno enabled unauthorized vocal replicas and violated Tennessee’s ELVIS Act. Their complaint also accuses the company of using copyrighted Presley material without permission.

Suno defended its platform in a statement to Billboard.

“Suno exists to help people create new, original music, not to trade on anyone’s name or likeness, and we prohibit any unauthorized use of an artist’s work. To protect against this, we do not allow prompts for specific artists’ names and songs and work with third party providers to screen uploaded audio files and lyrics for potential misuse. We are always working to strengthen our guardrails and we will continue to add new safeguards that protect artists and our users.”

The complaints challenge what happens when technology allegedly draws from that work to produce competing material.

Eight Mile Style seeks compensation for compositions while Presley’s rights owners are also defending his vocal identity. Their claims now await answers in court, where the dispute will turn on evidence rather than how convincingly a machine can deliver a familiar sound.

item.title: Killer Mike Celebrates Keisha Lance Bottoms’ Historic Georgia Victory
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Killer Mike joined Keisha Lance Bottoms' celebration after Georgia voters elected the nation's first Black woman governor.
item.content:encoded:
Killer Mike stepped onto the stage as Keisha Lance Bottoms celebrated a landmark victory in Georgia’s gubernatorial race.

The Atlanta rapper and longtime political activist joined supporters after voters elected Bottoms as the first Black woman to become a governor anywhere in the United States. 11Alive reported that Killer Mike had campaigned for prominent Georgia Democrats before addressing the crowd.

“They said it was impossible,” Killer Mike said. “Next election show them it’s possible again.”

Bottoms defeated Republican businessman Rick Jackson to become Georgia’s 84th governor. The former Atlanta mayor also became the first Democrat to win the state’s top office since 1998. Her victory added a national milestone to a political career already shaped by Atlanta City Hall and the White House.

The result followed two campaigns in which Stacey Abrams became the first Black woman to win a major party nomination for governor. Bottoms turned that unfinished history into a statewide victory.

Killer Mike’s place at the celebration carried a clear hometown connection. The Run The Jewels member has spent years mixing music with public arguments about voting, local ownership and political power.

Georgia lawmakers honored him at the state Capitol in 2025 for his music, civic work and economic impact in Atlanta.

He was also one of the most visible Atlanta artists supporting Democratic candidates during the midterm campaign. His appearance placed Hip-Hop inside a victory party that reflected how much metro Atlanta has changed the state’s political map.

Bottoms ran on plans to expand Medicaid, raise Georgia’s minimum wage and increase pay for teachers and other public employees. She also promised to challenge policies from President Donald Trump’s administration.

Those goals will depend on what she can move through a legislature where Republicans may retain control of at least one chamber.

The campaign overcame a major spending gap after Jackson put more than $200 million of his own fortune into the race. Bottoms won with about 54 percent of the vote and will succeed term-limited Governor Brian Kemp.

Killer Mike’s short message looked beyond one election night. His call to make the next unlikely win possible turned the celebration into an argument for continued political work across Georgia.

item.title: Pusha T Criticizes Rap’s Shift From Individuality To Imitation
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Pusha T says modern rap rewards imitation over individuality as Clipse's Grammy-winning reunion extends his run.
item.content:encoded:
Pusha T believes rap’s biggest problem is not a shortage of talent. It is a shortage of artists willing to stand apart.

The Clipse rapper made the case while discussing his daily life, competition and longevity with The Wall Street Journal. He said the culture once treated difference as the point, not a risk.

“It started off with a lot more individuality. Everybody wanted to be different. They wanted to be great, and they wanted to set themselves apart.”

Pusha T contrasted that mentality with a rap economy built around quick versions of whatever is already moving. In his view, artists can now earn attention while sounding and looking like the people beside them.

That may create a crowded field of competent records, but it does not create many distinct voices.

His own schedule is built around the opposite idea. He wakes around 5 A.M., often works 12-hour studio days and is usually in bed by 9 P.M.

The rigid routine comes during one of the strongest stretches of his career. Pusha T and Malice reunited as Clipse after 16 years, released Let God Sort Em Out, toured and won the duo’s first Grammy.

That comeback also gives Pusha T some evidence for his argument. Clipse did not chase a younger act’s sound to reenter the conversation. The brothers leaned into the sharp writing, restraint and tension that made their records recognizable in the first place.

He also pushed back on the idea that rap rivalries should disappear because online fan bases can turn competition ugly.

His line is simple: disagreement is part of the sport, but it should stay in the music. Anything beyond the record is where competition becomes reckless.

Pusha T’s long partnership with Pharrell Williams remains central to that work. The two recently launched Grindin’ Coffee, another extension of a friendship that began in Virginia Beach long before either had a hit.

“Probably the breadth of our friendship was based on music,” Pharrell told Vogue. Pusha T added, “My earliest memory of our friendship was acting like we went to school that day.”

Their early-morning calls and long studio shifts now feel less like nostalgia and more like a working system. Pusha T is betting that discipline, competition and an identifiable voice can still outlast the trend of the week.

item.title: Peter Gunz Wants Personal Issues Settled Before Recording With Lord Tariq
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Peter Gunz kept a Lord Tariq recording reunion open while revisiting personal issues and his past clash with Cardi B on "Drink Champs."
item.content:encoded:
Peter Gunz remained open to making music with Lord Tariq again, but he said personal and family issues needed to be settled before the Bronx duo could move forward together.

On episode 522 of “Drink Champs,” released November 6, Gunz explained what stood between the longtime partners and another collaboration.

“We got to straighten out a few family issues, a few things, personal things that happened,” he said.

Lord Tariq and Peter Gunz formed their duo in 1996 after working under the Gunrunners name. Both also built careers outside the partnership: Tariq with Money Boss Players and Gunz on Shaquille O’Neal’s T.W.is.M. label.

They signed with Columbia and broke through with “Deja Vu (Uptown Baby),” their 1997 single built around a Steely Dan sample. The record reached the pop Top 10 and remains the signature hit from their partnership. Their only album followed the next year.

Make It Reign arrived June 2, 1998. Its tracks included “Cross Bronx Expressway” with Fat Joe and Big Pun, “Streets To Da Stage” with Cam’ron and “Be My Lady” with Jermaine Paul and Jermaine Dupri.

Gunz described Tariq as a brother and one of his favorite rappers alongside his son Cory Gunz. He also said Tariq valued his privacy and disliked “Love & Hip Hop.”

Reality television became another major part of Gunz’s public life through “Love & Hip Hop” and his relationship with Amina Buddafly. The franchise also helped introduce Cardi B to a wider audience before her rap career took off.

Cardi and Gunz clashed over his treatment of women during a 2016 reunion. Both publicly acknowledged apologizing to each other that March.

In May, VH1 announced a six-part retrospective, “Love & Hip Hop: The Final Chapter,” for fall 2026. The special was designed to look back at 15 years of cast members across the franchise’s different cities.

Gunz revisited their reconciliation in the same episode and said he had been wrong to doubt her music prospects. That experience changed how he viewed younger rappers. He also made his support for her clear.

“I root for Cardi B. I love Cardi B,” Gunz said.

item.title: Detail Ordered Back To Court As Sexual Assault Case Enters Seventh Year
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Producer Detail is due back in court in February as his long-running sexual assault case continues in Los Angeles County.
item.content:encoded:
Grammy-winning producer Detail is due back in a Los Angeles courtroom on February 19 as his sexual assault case moves into a seventh year without a trial.

Noel Christopher Fisher has remained in Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department custody since his August 5, 2020 arrest. He now faces 29 charges involving multiple alleged victims, according to the Santa Clarita Valley Signal.

Detail has pleaded not guilty. The next hearing follows a defense effort to challenge the case earlier this year.

Judge Larry Fidler rejected a motion from attorney Andrew Flier arguing that Detail’s previous counsel had been ineffective and questioning whether the evidence supported sending some counts to trial.

One sexual battery count was dismissed, leaving the remaining charges in place.

Prosecutors opposed further delays. In a filing cited by the Signal, the Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office described “numerous acts of sexual abuse against multiple victims who have been waiting for years for the resolution of this case.”

The allegations span 2010 through 2018. When the case was first filed in 2020, prosecutors accused Detail of assaults involving six women between the ages of 18 and 31 at the time of the alleged incidents.

The original charges included forcible rape, forcible oral copulation, sodomy by force, assault and false imprisonment by violence.

The criminal complaint later expanded as additional women came forward.

Detail was held to answer after a 2021 preliminary hearing. His defense has since changed attorneys and sought more time to review a large record that includes multiple alleged victims, witnesses outside the United States and extensive digital material.

The producer has been held while the case proceeds. His work before the arrest included Beyoncé and JAY-Z’s “Drunk In Love,” Lil Wayne’s “How To Love,” Wiz Khalifa’s “We Dem Boyz” and records with Nicki Minaj, Future and Jennifer Lopez.

AllHipHop reported on his arrest in 2020.

A separate civil case produced a $15 million default judgment for Kristina Buch in 2019 after she accused Detail of rape and physical abuse. An appellate panel later upheld that judgment. The criminal prosecution remains pending, with Fisher’s next appearance now set for February 19.

item.title: Gervonta Davis Settles Civil Lawsuit Over Strip Club Allegations
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Gervonta Davis settled Courtney Rossel's civil lawsuit, ending her claims while his related criminal case remains active.
item.content:encoded:
Gervonta “Tank” Davis has settled the civil lawsuit filed by his former girlfriend over an alleged October 2025 confrontation at a Miami Gardens strip club.

Courtney Rossel voluntarily dismissed all of her claims with prejudice Thursday in Miami-Dade County. Her attorney, Richard Wolfe, confirmed the settlement to USA Today and said the “terms of the settlement are confidential.”

The dismissal prevents Rossel from refiling the same civil claims.

Rossel sued Davis on October 30, 2025, three days after the alleged encounter at Tootsie’s Cabaret.

She accused him of battery, aggravated battery, false imprisonment, kidnapping and intentional infliction of emotional distress. Rossel said she was working as a VIP cocktail waitress when Davis grabbed her and forced her through the club toward a parking area.

Her complaint sought compensatory and punitive damages along with a jury trial. The November 5 dismissal notice ended those civil claims before a trial, and the court filing did not disclose a payment figure or describe any other part of the agreement.

The allegations also brought a criminal investigation. Miami Gardens police obtained a warrant in January, and Davis was arrested later that month after a two-week search involving the U.S. Marshals Service.

He was released on bond and ordered to stay away from Rossel while the case moved forward.

The lawsuit put a major interruption into Davis’ boxing career. A planned exhibition fight with Jake Paul was canceled after the allegations surfaced.

Davis has not fought since his March 2025 majority draw with Lamont Roach Jr., and the WBA stripped him of its lightweight title in June after a mandatory bout did not happen.

The settlement closes Rossel’s civil case, while the criminal prosecution tied to the same alleged incident remains active. Davis still faces battery and kidnapping charges in Florida.

His next criminal status hearing is scheduled for November 17.

Prosecutors dropped a false-imprisonment charge in March after determining it overlapped with the kidnapping count. Davis previously entered not-guilty pleas in the pending case.

The court record did not disclose the civil settlement amount or other terms. Davis’ lawyer did not respond to the main report’s request for comment.

item.title: Diddy’s Daughter Love Asks When He Will Visit
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Love Sean Combs sent Sean "Diddy" Combs a birthday song and asked when he would visit as he serves a 50-month sentence.
item.content:encoded:
Love Sean Combs marked her father’s 57th birthday with a message that put their distance front and center.

Sean “Diddy” Combs’ 4-year-old daughter appeared in a video shared through her Instagram account.

“Hey daddy, it’s me, Love. I want to wish you a happy birthday! I miss you so much,” she said.

Love then asked when her father would visit, what he had eaten and what he had done that day. She sang “Happy Birthday” and showed a drawing labeled “Daddy” while “Bad Boy for Life” played in the background. The clip offered a child’s view of a prison sentence that has otherwise been discussed through court filings, appeals and release-date calculations.

Love was born in 2022 and is the youngest of Combs’ seven children. Her brief video stood apart from the legal updates because it documented how the separation is landing inside the family rather than arguing about the verdict or sentence.

Combs’ twin daughters, D’Lila and Jessie, also posted a birthday tribute. “Happy birthday to the best dad ever!!! We love and miss you so much and we wish we could celebrate with you on your special day!” they wrote.

The birthday messages arrived days after another change in Combs’ federal custody. He was moved from FCI Fort Dix in New Jersey to FCI Allenwood Low in Pennsylvania. His projected release date is now February 6, 2028, although projected dates can change as the Bureau of Prisons applies sentence credits and other calculations.

Combs is serving a 50-month sentence after a federal jury found him guilty in July 2025 on two counts of transporting people for prostitution. Jurors acquitted him of racketeering conspiracy and sex trafficking charges.

The Justice Department said it imposed the sentence on October 3, 2025. His lawyers have continued to challenge the case through the appeals process.

Federal officials confirmed the latest transfer but did not give a public reason, citing privacy and security concerns. The new facility remains a low-security prison, and the move did not end the sentence separating Combs from his youngest child.

Love’s message did not address the case. It stayed focused on the questions a child would ask: how her father spent his birthday and when she could see him again.

item.title: Yung Miami Had The Hit. What Happened With His New Album?
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: Yung Miami’s dismal debut raises questions about why “Spend Dat” listeners did not help Watch Dis.
item.content:encoded:
Yung Miami probably didn’t picture No. 138 when she named her debut solo album Watch Dis, but that is the Billboard 200 entrance being reported for Caresha’s big musical statement. Now comes the uncomfortable question: How did such a successful single lead to such a modest album opening?

Because “Spend Dat” certainly did its job. According to Universal Music’s album announcement, the record earned platinum certification and peaked at No. 17 on the Billboard Hot 100. That is a substantial achievement for somebody trying to establish herself outside City Girls. The invitation went out. Apparently, everybody didn’t stay for dinner.

Several outlets have reported approximately 10,500 opening units, but album equivalent units include streaming activity. So calling that number 10,500 albums “sold” is pretty misleading. We can discuss a disappointing chart entrance, numbers aside.

The album certainly wasn’t short on recognizable guests. Travis Scott, Summer Walker, Quavo, Bryson Tiller, Rick Ross, Trina and Trick Daddy appear across the project. For accuracy, Travis and Summer are album collaborators. The official “Spend Dat” remix features Lil Baby and Kodak Black, while the international version brings in Davido, Shenseea and Vybz Kartel.

That leaves me wondering whether people embraced the song more than the prospect of a full Caresha album. It happens. Knowing every word to one hook does not automatically mean somebody wants 21 tracks. A feature list can get listeners curious, but the repeat button requires a separate commitment.

Still, Hip-Hop’s obsession with declaring somebody finished after one opening week gets exhausting. A low debut deserves scrutiny. It also leaves room for another song to connect, a performance to change perceptions or listeners to discover something they initially overlooked.

My question is what Caresha does next. Which record gets the push? Does she lean into the party music or give the more personal material some attention?

She asked us to watch. The follow through may be more revealing than the opening number.

item.title: Queen Latifah Brings Newark Housing Mission To BET Documentary
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Queen Latifah's Newark housing effort takes center stage in You Can Go Home Again, premiering November 27 on BET.
item.content:encoded:
Queen Latifah‘s effort to build housing in Newark is headed to BET, which set a Friday, November 27 premiere for “You Can Go Home Again.”

The documentary follows the rapper’s return to the New Jersey community that raised her and the years of work behind RISE Living. The mixed-use development includes affordable apartments, with a name that honors her late mother, Rita.

BET announced that the film will air at 10 p.m. Eastern on the Friday after Thanksgiving. Muta’Ali directed it, with Flavor Unit Entertainment and P&G Studios co-producing.

“It’s about my community and the people and places that make us who we are,” Queen Latifah said.

RISE stands for Rita Is Still Everywhere. Latifah’s mother was a schoolteacher, and the film connects that family history with her investment in the neighborhood.

The housing effort predates the documentary announcement by years. Latifah joined Newark Mayor Ras Baraka for an April 2022 groundbreaking after construction had begun that January. Her BlueSugar Corporation worked with Life Assets Development and Gonsosa on the project.

Plans at the time called for 76 homes, including 16 classified as affordable. The rest included market-rate housing. That distinction is part of the project’s design: RISE was planned as a mixed-use development with affordable units within a larger residential community.

The plans also reserved 1,900 square feet on the ground floor for nonprofit organizations. They included a business center, fitness space and electric-vehicle charging stations, along with in-unit laundry and common-area Wi-Fi. Those were features outlined during the 2022 development phase.

The documentary received a first look in Chicago on November 4, when Latifah appeared with childhood friend and project partner Tammy Hammond at the Obama Presidential Center.

It also extends her work with a network where she now has a role beyond the screen. In June, Latifah and LL Cool J joined BET’s first advisory board. Her television and film production business includes Flavor Unit, which she runs with Shakim Compere.

Compere and Loretha Jones served as executive producers on “You Can Go Home Again.” The film follows the housing work alongside Latifah’s early life in Newark.
